thread.title: US STOCKS-Amazon jitters offset upbeat jobs data on Wall Street By Reuters

author: Reuters
title: US STOCKS-Amazon jitters offset upbeat jobs data on Wall Street By Reuters
text:
© Reuters. US STOCKS-Amazon jitters offset upbeat jobs data on Wall Street * Amazon drops after sales forecast misses estimates
* January payrolls rise more than expected
* Oil prices, strong earnings boost energy sector
* Indexes: Dow up 0.15 pct, S&P down 0.06 pct, Nasdaq off 0.35 pct (Updates to afternoon)
By Noel Randewich
Feb 1 (Reuters) - Wall Street was mixed on Friday, as optimism from a surge in January U.S. job growth was offset by a weaker-than-expected outlook from Amazon.com Inc AMZN.O that battered retail stocks.
The online retail heavyweight fell 5.3 percent after its quarterly sales forecast fell short of Wall Street estimates, overshadowing its record sales and profit during the holiday season. results put the Nasdaq in negative territory, while retailers Walmart (NYSE: WMT ) Inc WMT.N and Kohl's Corp KSS.N dropped more than 2 percent and Macy's Inc M.N fell 1.7 percent. The S&P consumer discretionary index .SPLRCD fell 1.8 percent.
A U.S. Labor Department report showed nonfarm payrolls jumped by 304,000 jobs last month, the largest gain since February 2018 and beating economists' expectations for an increase of 165,000. report, along with better-than-expected ISM manufacturing activity numbers for January, pointed to underlying strength in the economy despite an uncertain outlook that has left the Federal Reserve wary about more interest rate hikes this year.
“What the unemployment report is telling you is that people want to go back to work,” said Tom Martin, senior portfolio manager at GlobAlt Investments in Atlanta. “The consumer needs to be strong, and if the consumer is employed, the consumer will stay strong.”
Even as the United States remains on a steady footing, investors are concerned that a slowdown overseas could hurt profit growth, with high-profile companies such as Apple Inc AAPL.O warning of slowing demand in China.
Data showed China's manufacturing sector shrank for the second straight month in January, heightening risks for global growth amid a trade war with United States. 2:14 p.m. ET (1914 GMT), the Dow Jones Industrial Average .DJI was up 0.15 percent at 25,037.53 points, while the S&P 500 .SPX had lost 0.06 percent to 2,702.38.
The Nasdaq Composite .IXIC dropped 0.35 percent to 7,255.92.
Exxon Mobil Corp (NYSE: XOM ) XOM.N and Chevron Corp (NYSE: CVX ) CVX.N jumped more than 3 percent after the oil majors reported better-than-expected quarterly profits, boosting the Dow Jones industrial index. S&P energy index .SPNY rallied 1.78 percent, also helped by higher oil prices.
Cigna Corp (NYSE: CI ) CI.N fell 2.4 percent after the health insurer forecast 2019 revenue and earnings below estimates. S&P real estate index .SPLRCR dropped 1.3 percent.
Advancing issues outnumbered declining ones on the NYSE by a 1.22-to-1 ratio; on Nasdaq, a 1.30-to-1 ratio favored advancers.
The S&P 500 posted 29 new 52-week highs and no new lows; the Nasdaq Composite recorded 48 new highs and 15 new lows.
